title: Simulated Onsite Probe + 90d Activation Template
content:
Purpose:
This working template defines a lightweight simulated-onsite (pairing + system probe) used for mid-senior engineering hires. It combines an interview rubric, an actionable hiring decision rubric, and a first-90-day activation checklist that hiring managers can hand off after offer.

Scope and intent:
- Replace multi-hour whiteboard-only onsites with a 90–120 minute realistic pairing simulation that mirrors day-1 work.
- Surface collaboration, problem framing, and practical system tradeoffs (not only algorithmic puzzle solving).
- Produce a clear pass/fail + calibrated development runway for new hires (30/60/90 objectives).

Who should use this doc:
- People Ops interview coordinators (to book and prep panels)
- Hiring managers (to book tasks and interpret rubric)
- Interviewers (as a facilitator checklist)

Roles and responsibilities (quick):
- Facilitator: People Ops or designated interviewer — sets expectations, runs timer, ensures candidate has materials.
- Pairing interviewer: same-level engineer — does hands-on pairing, asks questions, takes notes.
- System interviewer: senior engineer or tech lead — leads design discussion and tradeoff probes.
- Hiring manager: observes (optional) and owns outcome + 90d plan if hire.

Simulated-onsite flow (recommended, 100–120 minutes):
1) Welcome & context (5 minutes) — quick intro, agenda, role call, pragmatic ask: "We want to see how you collaborate on a real bug/feature."
2) Warm-up and environment check (5 minutes) — confirm IDE/tooling, share repo link or sandbox.
3) Pairing task (40 minutes) — small end-to-end task that includes: reproduce bug or implement a feature in a simplified service, write testable code, and ship a PR-level diff. Candidate drives while interviewer prompts.
4) System probe / design follow-up (25 minutes) — evolve the pairing task to production scale: latency constraints, caching, routing, failure modes. Ask candidate to sketch APIs and rollout strategy.
5) Edge cases, ownership & tradeoffs (15 minutes) — product sense, monitoring, alerting syllabus, who owns what.
6) Calibration questions and candidate questions (10 minutes)
7) Debrief notes & interviewer sync (10 minutes) — quick consensus and log scores.

Interview materials (prep checklist):
- Minimal repo (private snippet) with failing tests and small dataset. Link pre-provisioned.
- Design prompt doc with measurable SLOs and a few hints.
- Recording template for notes + rubric scores.
- Candidate-mail templates (pre and post interview).

Scoring rubric (1–5, where 1 = major gaps, 3 = meets expectations, 5 = exceptional). Call out core vs support categories.
- Core (must not have 2s in more than one core):
  - Problem decomposition (core): 1–5 — breaks down work into incremental, testable steps.
  - Code correctness & testability (core): 1–5 — produces working, maintainable code with tests or clear testing plan.
  - Ownership & operational thinking (core): 1–5 — anticipates monitoring, rollouts, and incident vectors.
- Support:
  - System design and tradeoffs: 1–5 — clear tradeoffs, scaling plan, caching choices.
  - Communication / collaboration: 1–5 — clarity, receptivity to feedback, partner-first language.
  - Product sense: 1–5 — prioritization, user impact tradeoffs.
  - Learning velocity (evidence): 1–5 — how quickly candidate incorporated feedback during pairing.

Hiring decision guidance (heuristic):
- Strong Hire: cores median >= 4 and no 1s; overall >= 4.
- Hire with IC plan: cores >= 3 and has 1x3 but clear growth plan; manager must accept 30/60/90 ramp with specific mentoring.
- Weak/Pass for later: cores >= 3 but support scores low or mismatch to role seniority; consider hire into stretch role or IC program.
- No hire: any core with 1 OR cores median <= 2.5 and no credible upward path in 90 days.

Calibration examples (scenarios):
- Candidate wrote a correct quick fix but missed telemetry: code 4, ownership 2 -> likely "Hire with IC plan" if manager willing to mentor on ops.
- Candidate produced a good design but failed to complete core pairing task (broke tests): code 2, decomposition 2 -> "No hire".

Post-interview artifacts (what to produce right after):
- Short 3-sentence summary for hiring committee (what problem, what candidate did, top strengths, top risks).
- Completed numeric rubric (all categories).
- PR link / snippet reference if candidate produced code.
- Suggested initial 30/60/90 milestones (manager draft).

30/60/90 Activation template (manager-owned; send to People Ops after offer acceptance)
- Week 0 (pre-start): set up accounts, repo access, 1:1 cadence schedule, first-week plan.
- 30 days (practical goals): ship 1 low-risk fix, onboard to CI, own one small API, pair with buddy on oncall runbook.
- 60 days (expand scope): lead a small feature or performance patch, own deploy lane, own 1–2 alerting rules.
- 90 days (expected impact): independently land a medium feature, respond to a production incident end-to-end, present a retro on tradeoffs made.

Onboarding checklist (pre-start -> day 30, tickable by manager):
- Accounts + SSO + laptop imaged.
- GitHub + internal repo access verified.
- Dev sandbox seeded with toy dataset and simple task linking to pairing exercise.
- Buddy assigned and first-week pairing schedule in calendar.
- Access to relevant runbooks and SLO dashboards.
- Security & compliance training scheduled.

Manager handoff template (copy into offer packet):
- Candidate strengths (3 bullets)
- Initial risks and mitigation plan (3 bullets)
- First three tickets to assign (concrete JIRA keys)
- Buddy (name + contact) and weekly sync slot

Acceptance signals vs red flags (quick):
- Signals: rapid uptake during pairing, asks clarifying product questions, ownership language, asks about metrics and ops.
- Red flags: repeated basic misunderstandings about async request/response, inability to reason about failure modes, consistently defers to interviewer without proposing options.

Notes to self / open questions (People Ops):
- Should we gate the pairing repo to avoid overfitting / shared solutions? (JIRA-1234)
- How to measure fairness across remote vs onsite candidates? add rubric normalization session weekly.
- Follow up: draft PR template for interview code (owner: Marco Li).

Audit & compliance: keep rubric + notes in candidate folder (private) for 2 years per hiring retention policy.

Appendix: quick email templates (copy/paste)
- Pre-interview: "Hi <candidate>, this interview will be a 100–120 minute pairing session. Please make sure your dev environment is ready; we'll provide a browser-based sandbox if needed. Expect a mix of coding and design conversation."
- Post-interview decline: succinct feedback including one positive and one growth area.

Revision log:
- 2025-08-12 Asha K. Patel: initial draft (pairing-first flow)
- 2026-01-15 Marco Li: added rubric calibration notes and compliance pointers
- 2026-02-03 Nina Alvarez: adjusted 30/60/90 milestones for mid-senior ICs

End of doc.
